SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State one reason why energy crisis remains a serious problem in many developing countries despite the abundance of energy resources in these countries. *[1 mark]*

Distinguish between;

(ii) fossil fuels and biofuels

(iii) primary and secondary sources of energy. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Reason (one needed):** these countries lack the capital, technology and infrastructure (power stations, refineries, transmission and distribution grids) needed to **exploit and deliver** the available resources to the population. (Other acceptable reasons: poor planning and management, corruption, political instability, reliance on imported fuel and refined products, high cost of connecting rural areas.)

(ii) **Fossil fuels** are formed from the remains of plants and animals buried and transformed by heat and pressure over millions of years (coal, crude oil, natural gas). They are **non-renewable**: they are used up much faster than they form, and burning them releases carbon dioxide.
**Biofuels** are made from recently living organic matter (plants, wood, animal waste, crop residues): bioethanol, biodiesel, biogas, firewood. They are **renewable** (the plants can be regrown within a few years or decades) and, over their life cycle, return roughly the carbon dioxide the plants took up.

(iii) **Primary sources** are energy sources found in nature and used as they are, or after extraction, without any conversion: coal, crude oil, natural gas, uranium, the Sun, wind, falling water, biomass.
**Secondary sources** are obtained by converting a primary source: electricity, petrol, diesel, coke, hydrogen, steam (they carry energy but are not found ready-made in nature).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Draw a block diagram of a fossil fuel electricity generation scheme *[4 marks]*

(ii) In order to reduce the environmental problems resulting from the generation of electricity from fossil fuels, a community decides to build a facility to convert solar energy directly into electrical energy. If they require $1.0\ \mathrm{MW}$ of power and the photovoltaic panel to be installed has an efficiency of $20\%$, calculate the effective surface area of the panel given that the solar constant in the community is $1.4\ \mathrm{kW\,m^{-2}}$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Block diagram (to be drawn by the candidate), each block joined to the next by an arrow, with the energy form carried along each arrow:**

$$\boxed{\text{Fuel store (coal, oil or gas)}} \xrightarrow{\text{chemical}} \boxed{\text{Furnace and boiler}} \xrightarrow{\text{heat, high-pressure steam}} \boxed{\text{Turbine}} \xrightarrow{\text{kinetic (rotation)}} \boxed{\text{Generator (alternator)}} \xrightarrow{\text{electrical}} \boxed{\text{Step-up transformer}} \longrightarrow \boxed{\text{Transmission lines (grid)}}$$

The fuel is burnt in the furnace to heat water in the boiler; the steam drives the turbine, which turns the alternator. The exhaust steam goes to a **condenser** (cooled by river water or a cooling tower) and the condensed water is pumped back to the boiler (feed pump), forming a closed loop. The transformer raises the voltage for transmission to reduce $I^{2}R$ losses.

(ii) Useful electrical power output $= \text{efficiency} \times \text{solar power received}$, and the solar power received is the solar constant (intensity) times the area:
$$P = \eta\,I\,A \;\Rightarrow\; A = \frac{P}{\eta I} = \frac{1.0\times10^{6}\ \mathrm{W}}{0.20\times1.4\times10^{3}\ \mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}} = 3.57\times10^{3}\ \mathrm{m^{2}}.$$

**Effective surface area $\approx 3.6\times10^{3}\ \mathrm{m^{2}}$** ($3570\ \mathrm{m^{2}}$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define each of the following phenomena and state a consequence of each.

(i) Greenhouse effect

(ii) Ozone depletion. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Greenhouse effect:** the warming of the Earth's surface and lower atmosphere that occurs because greenhouse gases (carbon dioxide, methane, water vapour, nitrous oxide) are transparent to the incoming short-wavelength solar radiation but absorb the long-wavelength infrared radiation emitted by the warm Earth and re-radiate part of it back to the surface.
*Consequence:* an increase in the greenhouse gas concentration (from burning fossil fuels, deforestation) enhances the effect, causing **global warming**: melting of ice caps and glaciers, rise of the sea level, flooding of coastal areas, changes in rainfall and more frequent droughts and extreme weather.

(ii) **Ozone depletion:** the reduction of the concentration of ozone ($\mathrm{O_3}$) in the stratosphere, caused mainly by chlorine and bromine atoms released from man-made compounds (chlorofluorocarbons, CFCs, halons), which break down ozone molecules catalytically, producing the "ozone hole" over the polar regions.
*Consequence:* more harmful ultraviolet radiation (UV-B) reaches the Earth's surface, causing more skin cancers and cataracts in humans, and damage to crops and to plankton.
